questions.heading: Most Entries of a Model Matrix Are Zero
questions.stem: A crew-scheduling model has 2,000 rows and 50,000 columns, and no row mentions more than 6 variables. At most how dense is its constraint matrix?

options.text: About 50%, since every variable appears in at least one row
options.says: Appearing somewhere is not density: each variable appears in a few rows out of 2,000, and the rest of its column is zero.

options.text: About 6%, since each row mentions six of its variables
options.says: Six is a count of entries, not a percentage: six of 50,000 entries per row are nonzero.

options.text: About 0.012%, since each row holds six of 50,000 entries
options.says: Right: at most 6 × 2,000 nonzeros among 2,000 × 50,000 entries is 6 / 50,000 = 0.012%.

options.text: About 4%, since the model has 2,000 rows for 50,000 columns
options.says: The ratio of rows to columns says nothing about how many entries of each row are nonzero.

questions.heading: Store Only the Nonzeros: Triplets, Then Compressed Rows
questions.stem: A CSR matrix has indptr = [0, 3, 3, 5] and indices = [1, 4, 6, 0, 2]. Counting rows from 0, which columns hold the nonzeros of row 2?

options.text: Columns 0 and 2, since row 2 owns positions 3 and 4
options.says: Right: row 2 runs from indptr[2] = 3 up to, not including, indptr[3] = 5, and indices[3:5] is [0, 2].

options.text: No columns, since the repeated 3 marks row 2 as empty
options.says: The repeated 3 is the end of row 0 and the start and end of row 1, so row 1 is the empty one.

options.text: Column 6 alone, since indices[2] holds the column of row 2
options.says: indices has one entry per nonzero, not per row; indptr says which of its positions belong to a row.

options.text: Columns 3 and 5, since indptr holds the columns of row 2
options.says: indptr holds positions in data and indices, not columns; the columns are read from indices.

questions.heading: Sparse Products Give the Same Answer in a Fraction of the Memory
questions.stem: Stored dense with 8-byte numbers, a model's constraint matrix takes 400 MB, and 0.1% of its entries are nonzero. CSR stores each value in 8 bytes and each column index in 8 bytes. About how much memory does the CSR form take?

options.text: About 400 MB, since CSR stores the same matrix as the dense form
options.says: It is the same matrix, but CSR leaves the zeros out, and they are 99.9% of the entries.

options.text: About 0.4 MB, since CSR keeps 0.1% of the dense form's values
options.says: That counts data only; CSR also stores a column index for every value, plus indptr.

options.text: About 200 MB, since CSR stores each row once instead of twice
options.says: CSR does not halve anything: its size follows the number of nonzeros, not the number of entries.

options.text: About 0.8 MB plus indptr, since each nonzero keeps a value and a column
options.says: Right: 50 million entries at 0.1% is 50,000 nonzeros, at 16 bytes each, plus one indptr entry per row.
